audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Gerasene release, Legion naming, return-home witness, Jairus, hemorrhaging woman, sozo as saved/healed, daughter language, fear/trust, and raising of Jairus' daughter.

verses.restored: They came to the other side of the sea, into the region of the Gerasenes.

familiar.text: And they came over unto the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.

modern.text: On the other side of the sea, they arrived in the region of the Gerasenes.

original.text: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν ⸀Γερασηνῶν.

verses.restored: Immediately, as he came out of the boat, a man in an unclean spirit met him from the tombs.

familiar.text: And when he was come out of the ship, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,

modern.text: As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, He was met by a man with an unclean spirit, who was coming from the tombs.

original.text: καὶ ⸂ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ⸃ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ⸂εὐθὺς ὑπήντησεν⸃ αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ,

verses.restored: He had his dwelling among the tombs, and no one was able to bind him anymore, not even with a chain.

familiar.text: Who had his dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains:

modern.text: This man had been living in the tombs and could no longer be restrained, even with chains.

original.text: ὃς τὴν κατοίκησιν εἶχεν ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν, καὶ ⸂οὐδὲ ἁλύσει οὐκέτι⸃ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο αὐτὸν δῆσαι

verses.restored: For he had often been bound with shackles and chains, but the chains were torn apart by him and the shackles crushed; no one was strong enough to tame him.

familiar.text: Because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him.

modern.text: Though he was often bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and shattered the shackles. Now there was no one with the strength to subdue him.

original.text: διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν πολλάκις πέδαις καὶ ἁλύσεσι δεδέσθαι καὶ διεσπάσθαι ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ τὰς ἁλύσεις καὶ τὰς πέδας συντετρῖφθαι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ⸂ἴσχυεν αὐτὸν⸃ δαμάσαι·

verses.restored: Night and day among the tombs and mountains he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.

familiar.text: And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.

modern.text: Night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones.

original.text: καὶ διὰ παντὸς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐν τοῖς ⸂μνήμασιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν⸃ ἦν κράζων καὶ κατακόπτων ἑαυτὸν λίθοις.

verses.restored: Seeing Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed/prostrated before him.

familiar.text: But when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and worshipped him,

modern.text: When the man saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and fell on his knees before Him.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἰδὼν⸃ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔδραμεν καὶ προσεκύνησεν ⸀αὐτόν,

verses.restored: Crying out with a great voice, he said, What to me and to you, Jesus, Son of the Most High Divine? I adjure you by the Divine: do not torment me.

familiar.text: And cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the most high God? I adjure thee by God, that thou torment me not.

modern.text: And he shouted in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You before God not to torture me!”

original.text: καὶ κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ⸀λέγει· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου; ὁρκίζω σε τὸν θεόν, μή με βασανίσῃς.

verses.restored: For Jesus had been saying to him, Come out from the man, unclean spirit.

familiar.text: For he said unto him, Come out of the man, thou unclean spirit.

modern.text: For Jesus had already declared, “Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!”

original.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ· Ἔξελθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

verses.restored: Jesus asked him, What is your name? He said to him, Legion is my name, because we are many.

familiar.text: And he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.

modern.text: “What is your name?” Jesus asked. “My name is Legion,” he replied, “for we are many.”

original.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Τί ⸂ὄνομά σοι⸃; καὶ ⸂λέγει αὐτῷ⸃· ⸀Λεγιὼν ὄνομά μοι, ὅτι πολλοί ἐσμεν·

verses.restored: He pleaded with him many times not to send them out of the region.

familiar.text: And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.

modern.text: And he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of that region.

original.text: καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἵνα μὴ ⸀αὐτὰ ἀποστείλῃ ἔξω τῆς χώρας.

verses.restored: Now there was there on the mountain a great herd of pigs feeding.

familiar.text: Now there was there nigh unto the mountains a great herd of swine feeding.

modern.text: There on the nearby hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding.

original.text: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πρὸς τῷ ὄρει ἀγέλη χοίρων μεγάλη βοσκομένη·

verses.restored: They pleaded with him, saying, Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter them.

familiar.text: And all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.

modern.text: So the demons begged Jesus, “Send us to the pigs, so that we may enter them.”

original.text: καὶ παρεκάλεσαν ⸀αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Πέμψον ἡμᾶς εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, ἵνα εἰς αὐτοὺς εἰσέλθωμεν.

verses.restored: He permitted them. The unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs; the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand, and were drowned in the sea.

familiar.text: And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea.

modern.text: He gave them permission, and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs, and the herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the water.

original.text: καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν ⸀αὐτοῖς. καὶ ἐξελθόντα τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ⸀ὡς δισχίλιοι, καὶ ἐπνίγοντο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.

verses.restored: Those feeding them fled and reported it in the city and in the fields; and people came to see what had happened.

familiar.text: And they that fed the swine fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done.

modern.text: Those tending the pigs ran off and reported this in the town and countryside, and the people went out to see what had happened.

original.text: ⸂Καὶ οἱ⸃ βόσκοντες ⸀αὐτοὺς ἔφυγον καὶ ⸀ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς· καὶ ⸀ἦλθον ἰδεῖν τί ἐστιν τὸ γεγονός.

verses.restored: They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been troubled by Legion sitting, clothed, and sound-minded; and they were afraid.

familiar.text: And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.

modern.text: When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

original.text: καὶ ἔρχονται πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ θεωροῦσιν τὸν δαιμονιζόμενον ⸀καθήμενον ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα, τὸν ἐσχηκότα τὸν ⸀λεγιῶνα, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.

verses.restored: Those who had seen explained to them what had happened to the man troubled by unclean spirits, and about the pigs.

familiar.text: And they that saw it told them how it befell to him that was possessed with the devil, and also concerning the swine.

modern.text: Those who had seen it described what had happened to the demon-possessed man and also to the pigs.

original.text: ⸂καὶ διηγήσαντο⸃ αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐγένετο τῷ δαιμονιζομένῳ καὶ περὶ τῶν χοίρων.

verses.restored: They began to plead with Jesus to depart from their borders.

familiar.text: And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts.

modern.text: And the people began to beg Jesus to leave their region.

original.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο παρακαλεῖν αὐτὸν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: As he was entering the boat, the one who had been troubled pleaded that he might be with him.

familiar.text: And when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him.

modern.text: As He was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by the demons begged to go with Him.

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἐμβαίνοντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πλοῖον παρεκάλει αὐτὸν ὁ δαιμονισθεὶς ἵνα ⸂μετʼ αὐτοῦ ᾖ⸃.

verses.restored: He did not permit him, but said, Go to your house, to your own people, and report to them how much the Lord has done for you and how he had mercy on you.

familiar.text: Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.

modern.text: But Jesus would not allow him. “Go home to your own people,” He said, “and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.”

original.text: ⸀καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου πρὸς τοὺς σούς, καὶ ⸀ἀπάγγειλον αὐτοῖς ὅσα ⸂ὁ κύριός σοι⸃ πεποίηκεν καὶ ἠλέησέν σε.

verses.restored: He went away and began proclaiming in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone marveled.

familiar.text: And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men did marvel.

modern.text: So the man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed. The Healing Touch of Jesus (Matthew 9:18–26; Luke 8:40–56)

original.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν ἐν τῇ Δεκαπόλει ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ πάντες ἐθαύμαζον.

verses.restored: When Jesus crossed again in the boat to the other side, a great crowd gathered around him, and he was beside the sea.

familiar.text: And when Jesus was passed over again by ship unto the other side, much people gathered unto him: and he was nigh unto the sea.

modern.text: When Jesus had again crossed by boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him beside the sea.

original.text: Καὶ διαπεράσαντος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ πάλιν εἰς τὸ πέραν συνήχθη ὄχλος πολὺς ἐπʼ αὐτόν, καὶ ἦν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν.

verses.restored: One of the synagogue rulers came, Jairus by name, and seeing him, fell at his feet.

familiar.text: And, behold, there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet,

modern.text: A synagogue leader named Jairus arrived, and seeing Jesus, he fell at His feet

original.text: ⸀καὶ ἔρχεται εἷς τῶν ἀρχισυναγώγων, ὀνόματι Ἰάϊρος, καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν πίπτει πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ

verses.restored: He pleaded with him many times, saying, My little daughter is at the point of death; come lay hands on her, so that she may be saved/healed and live.

familiar.text: And besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: I pray thee, come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live.

modern.text: and pleaded with Him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Please come and place Your hands on her, so that she will be healed and live.”

original.text: καὶ ⸀παρακαλεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ λέγων ὅτι Τὸ θυγάτριόν μου ἐσχάτως ἔχει, ἵνα ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς ⸂τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ⸃ ⸀ἵνα σωθῇ καὶ ⸀ζήσῃ.

verses.restored: Jesus went with him, and a great crowd followed him and pressed around him.

familiar.text: And Jesus went with him; and much people followed him, and thronged him.

modern.text: So Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed around Him.

original.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς, καὶ συνέθλιβον αὐτόν.

verses.restored: A woman was there with a flow of blood twelve years.

familiar.text: And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years,

modern.text: And a woman was there who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.

original.text: καὶ ⸀γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος ⸂δώδεκα ἔτη⸃

verses.restored: She had suffered much under many physicians and spent all she had, yet was not helped but rather became worse.

familiar.text: And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,

modern.text: She had borne much agony under the care of many physicians and had spent all she had, but to no avail. Instead, her condition had only grown worse.

original.text: καὶ πολλὰ παθοῦσα ὑπὸ πολλῶν ἰατρῶν καὶ δαπανήσασα τὰ παρʼ αὐτῆς πάντα καὶ μηδὲν ὠφεληθεῖσα ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εἰς τὸ χεῖρον ἐλθοῦσα,

verses.restored: Having heard about Jesus, she came behind him in the crowd and touched his garment.

familiar.text: When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment.

modern.text: When the woman heard about Jesus, she came up through the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak.

original.text: ⸀ἀκούσασα περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλθοῦσα ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: For she was saying, If I touch even his garments, I will be saved/healed.

familiar.text: For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.

modern.text: For she kept saying, “If only I touch His garments, I will be healed.”

original.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὅτι ⸂Ἐὰν ἅψωμαι κἂν τῶν ἱματίων αὐτοῦ⸃ σωθήσομαι.

verses.restored: Immediately the spring of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been healed from the affliction.

familiar.text: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague.

modern.text: Immediately her bleeding stopped, and she sensed in her body that she was healed of her affliction.

original.text: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἐξηράνθη ἡ πηγὴ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς, καὶ ἔγνω τῷ σώματι ὅτι ἴαται ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγος.

verses.restored: Immediately Jesus, knowing in himself that power had gone out from him, turned in the crowd and said, Who touched my garments?

familiar.text: And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes?

modern.text: At once Jesus was aware that power had gone out from Him. Turning to the crowd, He asked, “Who touched My garments?”

original.text: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐπιγνοὺς ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἐξ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν ἐξελθοῦσαν ἐπιστραφεὶς ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ἔλεγεν· Τίς μου ἥψατο τῶν ἱματίων;

verses.restored: His disciples said to him, You see the crowd pressing around you, and you say, Who touched me?

familiar.text: And his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?

modern.text: His disciples answered, “You can see the crowd pressing in on You, and yet You ask, ‘Who touched Me?’”

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ· Βλέπεις τὸν ὄχλον συνθλίβοντά σε, καὶ λέγεις· Τίς μου ἥψατο;

verses.restored: He looked around to see the one who had done this.

familiar.text: And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.

modern.text: But He kept looking around to see who had done this.

original.text: καὶ περιεβλέπετο ἰδεῖν τὴν τοῦτο ποιήσασαν.

verses.restored: The woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came, fell before him, and told him all the truth.

familiar.text: But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

modern.text: Then the woman, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before Him trembling in fear, and she told Him the whole truth.

original.text: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ φοβηθεῖσα καὶ τρέμουσα, εἰδυῖα ὃ γέγονεν ⸀αὐτῇ, ἦλθεν καὶ προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν.

verses.restored: He said to her, Daughter, your trust has saved/healed you. Go into peace, and be whole from your affliction.

familiar.text: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.

modern.text: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· ⸀Θυγάτηρ, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· ὕπαγε εἰς εἰρήνην, καὶ ἴσθι ὑγιὴς ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγός σου.

verses.restored: While he was still speaking, some came from the synagogue ruler's house, saying, Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher still?

familiar.text: While he yet spake, there came from the ruler of the synagogue’s house certain which said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further?

modern.text: While He was still speaking, messengers from the house of Jairus arrived and said, “Your daughter is dead; why bother the Teacher anymore?”

original.text: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχονται ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ σου ἀπέθανεν· τί ἔτι σκύλλεις τὸν διδάσκαλον;

verses.restored: But Jesus, overhearing the word spoken, said to the synagogue ruler, Do not fear; only trust.

familiar.text: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.

modern.text: But Jesus overheard their conversation and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸀παρακούσας τὸν λόγον λαλούμενον λέγει τῷ ἀρχισυναγώγῳ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, μόνον πίστευε.

verses.restored: He did not allow anyone to follow with him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

familiar.text: And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.

modern.text: And He did not allow anyone to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν οὐδένα ⸂μετʼ αὐτοῦ⸃ συνακολουθῆσαι εἰ μὴ ⸀τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰακώβου.

verses.restored: They came to the house of the synagogue ruler, and he saw a commotion, people weeping and wailing loudly.

familiar.text: And he cometh to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.

modern.text: When they arrived at the house of the synagogue leader, Jesus saw the commotion and the people weeping and wailing loudly.

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἔρχονται εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου, καὶ θεωρεῖ θόρυβον ⸀καὶ κλαίοντας καὶ ἀλαλάζοντας πολλά,

verses.restored: Entering, he said to them, Why do you make commotion and weep? The child has not died but sleeps.

familiar.text: And when he was come in, he saith unto them, Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth.

modern.text: He went inside and asked, “Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead, but asleep.”

original.text: καὶ εἰσελθὼν λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί θορυβεῖσθε καὶ κλαίετε; τὸ παιδίον οὐκ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει.

verses.restored: They laughed at him. But he put them all outside, took the child's father and mother and those with him, and entered where the child was.

familiar.text: And they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and entereth in where the damsel was lying.

modern.text: And they laughed at Him. After He had put them all outside, He took the child’s father and mother and His own companions, and went in to see the child.

original.text: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ. ⸀αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκβαλὼν πάντας παραλαμβάνει τὸν πατέρα τοῦ παιδίου καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τοὺς μετʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἰσπορεύεται ὅπου ἦν τὸ ⸀παιδίον·

verses.restored: Taking the child's hand, he said to her, Talitha koum, which is translated, Little girl, I say to you, rise.

familiar.text: And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.

modern.text: Taking her by the hand, Jesus said, “Talitha koum!” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!”

original.text: καὶ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ παιδίου λέγει αὐτῇ· Ταλιθα ⸀κουμ, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον· Τὸ κοράσιον, σοὶ λέγω, ⸀ἔγειρε.

verses.restored: Immediately the girl rose and walked, for she was twelve years old. Immediately they were overcome with great amazement.

familiar.text: And straightway the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment.

modern.text: Immediately the girl got up and began to walk around. She was twelve years old, and at once they were utterly astounded.

original.text: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἀνέστη τὸ κοράσιον καὶ περιεπάτει, ἦν γὰρ ἐτῶν δώδεκα. καὶ ἐξέστησαν ⸁εὐθὺς ἐκστάσει μεγάλῃ.

verses.restored: He strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and said that something should be given her to eat.

familiar.text: And he charged them straitly that no man should know it; and commanded that something should be given her to eat.

modern.text: Then Jesus gave strict orders that no one should know about this, and He told them to give her something to eat.

original.text: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἵνα μηδεὶς γνοῖ τοῦτο, καὶ εἶπεν δοθῆναι αὐτῇ φαγεῖν.
